rationale: The unit opens on the header that begins Agur's collection, דִּבְרֵ֤י ... הַמַּ֫שָּׂ֥א (oshb:Prov.30.1, "the words of Agur ... the oracle"), and runs through a first-person meditation on the limits of human knowledge before God (30:2-4) into an affirmation that God's own word is tested and trustworthy (30:5) and a warning not to add to it, אַל תּ֥וֹסְףְּ עַל דְּבָרָ֑יו (oshb:Prov.30.6, "do not add to his words"). The term for "words of" (דִּבְרֵ֤י) occurs anywhere in 19 verses book-wide (sweep: 19, oshb:Prov.30.1), opens the verse in 5 of those (sweep: 5 of 19, the verse-initial subset), and pairs with an oracle-word to form an actual collection header in only 2 of those 5 (sweep: 2 of 5) -- here and again at the Lemuel header. The petuchah recorded at oshb:Prov.30.6 (single-witness) corroborates this seam before the numbered petition that begins the next unit.
rejected_alternative: Splitting the divrei/massa header (30:1) into its own row was considered, since it alone carries the disputed Ithiel-Ucal reading, but the first-person voice of 30:1 continues without interruption into the confession of 30:2, so the header stays inside the unit it opens.
observed_substrate_signals: verse-initial header token דִּבְרֵ֤י paired with הַמַּ֫שָּׂ֥א at oshb:Prov.30.1
the doubled name-form לְאִֽיתִיאֵ֑ל לְאִ֖יתִיאֵ֣ל וְאֻכָֽל at oshb:Prov.30.1 (the Ithiel/Ucal crux; disclosed, reading not resolved here)
imperative closing warning אַל תּ֥וֹסְףְּ עַל דְּבָרָ֑יו at oshb:Prov.30.6

the confession spanning 30:2-5 opens without a numeral or vocative-address formula, unlike the numbered sayings later in the chapter
device_notes: Register is first-person confessional (30:2-5) framed by third-person narration about the speaker (30:1) and a second-person warning (30:6) -- parallelism class synthetic; descriptive texture, not the unit_type choice. Greek witnesses relocate this material: Agur's sayings move to sit beside the "words of the wise" appendix earlier in the book, and Lemuel's oracle moves beside them too, while the eshet-chayil poem remains at the book's end -- a cross-tradition fact about Greek ordering that does not bear on the MT/WEB boundaries argued in this span, which agree on one consistent order across chs 30-31.

rationale: A new petition formula opens with the numeral שְׁ֭תַּיִם (oshb:Prov.30.7, "two things"), distinct in voice and grammar from the confession that precedes it -- the petuchah at oshb:Prov.30.6 (single-witness, disclosed) marks that seam. The petition is unpacked through a request to be free of falsehood and of both poverty and riches (30:8), reasoned in 30:9 with a rhetorical question naming the divine name directly, מִ֥י יְה֫וָ֥ה (oshb:Prov.30.9, "who is Yahweh"), the sole occurrence of that exact token in this chapter (sweep: 1 of 70 book-wide). The petuchah at oshb:Prov.30.9 (single-witness, disclosed) closes the petition before the unrelated servant/slander saying that follows.
rejected_alternative: Some readers take 30:8-9 as unpacking one combined request rather than the two things named in 30:7, but the row boundary follows the explicit two-part numeral opening the petition, not a count of the clauses that follow it.
observed_substrate_signals: numeral opener שְׁ֭תַּיִם at oshb:Prov.30.7
divine-name question מִ֥י יְה֫וָ֥ה at oshb:Prov.30.9
petuchah brackets both ends of the unit (oshb:Prov.30.6 and oshb:Prov.30.9, both single-witness)
device_notes: The two-thing opening here anticipates the three/four formulas used later in the chapter's nature sayings, but unpacks two petitions rather than an itemized list of nouns -- texture distinguishing this saying's shape from the animal-list sayings, not a separate unit_type.

rationale: A self-contained admonition about household loyalty, אַל תַּלְשֵׁ֣ן עֶ֭בֶד (oshb:Prov.30.10, "do not slander a servant") to his אדנו/אֲדֹנָ֑יו (ketiv/qere pair, the unpointed form sitting inline before the pointed form at oshb:Prov.30.10), shares no anaphoric opening or catchword with the fourfold "generation" run that begins immediately after at web:Prov.30.11, so it stands as its own verse between the petuchah at oshb:Prov.30.9 (single-witness, disclosed) and that run.
rejected_alternative: Grouping this verse with the four "generation" sayings that follow was considered because both concern household or family disorder, but 30:10 opens with a prohibition rather than the repeated "generation" noun that binds 30:11-14 together, so it is kept separate.
observed_substrate_signals: prohibition opener אַל תַּלְשֵׁ֣ן at oshb:Prov.30.10 (ketiv/qere verse; the K/Q pair itself is the next signal)

device_notes: The inline unpointed-before-pointed ketiv/qere pattern at oshb:Prov.30.10 matches the book-wide kq layer's usual shape (69 notes total, sweep: 69) -- texture, not a boundary driver.

rationale: Four consecutive verses open with the identical word דּ֭וֹר (oshb:Prov.30.11-Prov.30.14, "a generation who..."), an anaphoric chain naming a byte-grounded construction-run (4 of 4 verses share the same opening token, sweep: 4 of 4) rather than a shared theme alone. The run closes on the sword-sense homograph חֲרָב֣וֹת שִׁנָּיו֮ (oshb:Prov.30.14, "teeth are like swords"), describing teeth rather than a foodstuff or a place-name -- distinct from the dry-morsel sense of the same root argued elsewhere at web:Prov.17.1. The petuchah at oshb:Prov.30.14 (single-witness, disclosed) corroborates the run's close before the leech saying at web:Prov.30.15.
rejected_alternative: Four separate single-verse rows were considered, since each "generation" line is grammatically complete on its own, but the identical opening word repeated across all four lines is exactly the kind of construction-run cohesion the collection's granularity rule treats as cluster-grade evidence, not a merely thematic grouping.

device_notes: Parallelism class synthetic/descriptive: the four lines (4 of 4) complete parallel portraits of arrogance or filial contempt, rather than contrasting two clauses; the anaphora itself, not the shared theme, is the cluster's cohesion evidence.

rationale: The leech's two daughters, שְׁתֵּ֥י בָנוֹת֮ (oshb:Prov.30.15, "two daughters"), pivot straight into the chapter's first explicit three/four formula, שָׁל֣וֹשׁ ... אַ֝רְבַּ֗ע (oshb:Prov.30.15, "three ... four"), whose four unsatisfied appetites -- Sheol, the barren womb, the earth, and fire -- are named in 30:16 alone (4 of 4 there, oshb:Prov.30.16). The petuchah at oshb:Prov.30.14 (single-witness, disclosed) opens the unit, and the layer records a mark at neither of its own two verses, so the numeral and its own list are kept together as one function unit.
rejected_alternative: Treating 30:15 and 30:16 as separate rows -- the leech image alone, then the four-item list alone -- was considered, but the four-thing tally opened in 30:15 (4 of 4) is not settled until 30:16 supplies its members, so splitting there would cut the numeral from its own list.

device_notes: Parallelism class list/enumerative -- four parallel nouns in apposition across 30:16; descriptive texture, not the unit_type label.

rationale: A self-contained warning about filial contempt, עַ֤יִן תִּֽלְעַ֣ג לְאָב֮ (oshb:Prov.30.17, "the eye that mocks a father"), punished by scavenging birds, carries no numeral opener and no anaphoric link to the "three/four" sayings either side of it (web:Prov.30.15-Prov.30.16 before, web:Prov.30.18-Prov.30.20 after). The petuchah at oshb:Prov.30.17 (single-witness, disclosed) closes it as its own segment.
rejected_alternative: Folding this verse into the following "three things too amazing" saying was considered on a shared theme of family disorder, but 30:17 opens with an image, not a numeral, and the petuchah closing 30:17 (disclosed) separates it from 30:18.

rationale: The chapter's second three/four formula opens the unit, שְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה ... וְ֝אַרְבָּעָ֗ה (oshb:Prov.30.18, "three ... four"; the "four" token sits as an unpointed ketiv וארבע directly before its pointed qere וְ֝אַרְבָּעָ֗ה, disclosed). Its fourth listed item -- "the way of a man with a maiden" -- is picked up by an explicit catchword chain: the noun for "way" opens all four items of 30:19 and is used a fifth time to open the comparison verse itself, כֵּ֤ן דֶּ֥רֶךְ אִשָּׁ֗ה (oshb:Prov.30.20, "so is the way of an adulterous woman"). The petuchah at oshb:Prov.30.17 (single-witness, disclosed) opens the unit and the petuchah at oshb:Prov.30.20 (single-witness, disclosed) closes it.
rejected_alternative: Setting 30:20 apart as an independent proverb about adultery was considered, since its subject differs from the nature-list of 30:19, but the fifth repetition of the same "way" noun ties it to the list as the formula's own application rather than a new topic.

ketiv/qere at the "four" token, oshb:Prov.30.18

device_notes: Parallelism class synthetic (list plus applied analogy); the repeated "way" noun is the cluster's own catchword-chain evidence.

rationale: The chapter's third three/four formula, שָׁ֭לוֹשׁ ... אַ֝רְבַּ֗ע (oshb:Prov.30.21, "three ... four"), states that the earth trembles under four things, then names all four across the next two verses: a servant becoming king and a fool filled with food in 30:22, an unloved woman married and a maidservant supplanting her mistress in 30:23. The petuchah at oshb:Prov.30.20 (single-witness, disclosed) opens the unit and the petuchah at oshb:Prov.30.23 (single-witness, disclosed) closes it, the list kept whole as one function unit.
rejected_alternative: Splitting 30:22 and 30:23 into separate rows was considered since each verse supplies two of the four items, but the numeral opened in 30:21 is not complete until both verses are read together.

rationale: A stated count of אַרְבָּ֣עָה (oshb:Prov.30.24, "four") small but wise creatures opens the unit, then itemizes exactly four across the following verses -- ants (30:25), rock badgers (30:26), locusts (30:27), and a lizard caught by hand yet found in a king's palace (30:28). A petuchah brackets both ends of the unit -- oshb:Prov.30.23 before it, oshb:Prov.30.28 after (both single-witness, disclosed) -- and the whole list is kept as one unit under the chapter's function-based chunking for its numbered sayings.
rejected_alternative: Breaking the list at its midpoint, after the ants and rock badgers, was considered to keep the row shorter, but a four-item numeral formula is one function unit and the chapter's numerical sayings are chunked by that function, not by length.

rationale: The chapter's final three/four formula, שְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה ... וְ֝אַרְבָּעָ֗ה (oshb:Prov.30.29, "three ... four"), names things stately in gait; the lion alone supplies one member of the count in 30:30 (1 of 4), and 30:31 packs the remaining three into one verse (3 of 4 there: a strutting animal, the male goat, and a king with his army), so the four-item count needs both verses read together. The petuchah at oshb:Prov.30.28 (single-witness, disclosed) opens the unit.
rejected_alternative: Extending this row through 30:32-33 was considered, since both continue the chapter's sequence of numbered and admonitory sayings, but the shift from third-person animal description to a second-person command at 30:32 is a plain register change kept separate here.

rationale: The unit shifts from third-person nature description to a direct second-person command, אִם נָבַ֥לְתָּ בְהִתְנַשֵּׂ֑א (oshb:Prov.30.32, "if you have acted foolishly in lifting yourself up"), closing with a plain call to silence, יָ֣ד לְפֶֽה (oshb:Prov.30.32, "a hand to the mouth"). Its motive clause in 30:33 repeats the same verb-noun three times, מִ֪יץ ... וּֽמִיץ ... וּמִ֥יץ (oshb:Prov.30.33, "pressing/churning"), so the admonition and its threefold rationale are read as one unit. The petuchah at oshb:Prov.30.33 (single-witness, disclosed) closes both this admonition and the chapter itself, right before the Lemuel collection begins.
rejected_alternative: Reading 30:32 as a further "stately" item closing the preceding animal list was considered, but the shift to second-person imperative address is a register change from the third-person descriptions used across the surrounding numbered sayings, so it is kept as its own admonition.

rationale: The unit opens on the book's second and final divrei-plus-massa header, דִּ֭בְרֵי לְמוּאֵ֣ל מֶ֑לֶךְ מַ֝שָּׂ֗א (oshb:Prov.31.1, "the words of Lemuel the king, an oracle"), matching web:Prov.30.1 in kind (the same opening token דִּ֭בְרֵי pairs with an oracle-word as an actual header in 2 of the 19 book-wide hits, sweep: 2 of 19) though never in wording. The mother's address that follows opens with a triple vocative on a short root, מַה בְּ֭רִי וּמַֽה בַּר בִּטְנִ֑י וּ֝מֶה בַּר נְדָרָֽי (oshb:Prov.31.2, "what, my son! what, son of my womb! what, son of my vows!") -- the later two vocatives here, בַּר and בַּר, use a short form beside the fuller בְּ֭רִי used earlier in the same verse; that short form is Aramaic-influenced address vocabulary, discussion material rather than a claim that the verse itself is in Aramaic (every morph code in the book is H-prefixed, sweep: 6984 of 6984). The same address continues through the warnings against wine and women (31:3-7, including the twice-repeated אַ֤ל לַֽמְלָכִ֨ים לְֽמוֹאֵ֗ל אַ֣ל לַֽמְלָכִ֣ים at oshb:Prov.31.4, ketiv/qere verse, "not for kings ... not for kings") into the closing charge to judge the poor justly (31:8-9); the petuchah at oshb:Prov.31.9 (single-witness, disclosed) is the unit's one interior mark, closing it right before the acrostic begins.
rejected_alternative: Splitting the wine warning (31:3-7) from the justice charge (31:8-9) into two admonition_unit rows was considered, since their imagery differs, but both remain inside the one address the mother opens in 31:2 and sustains across all seven verses to 31:8 (7 of 7), with the same vocative frame governing both.

rationale: The poem opens אֵֽשֶׁת חַ֭יִל (oshb:Prov.31.10, "a woman of strength"), a phrase that also occurs earlier in the book at web:Prov.12.4 (sweep: 2 book-wide), so its appearance here is not unique to this poem. Each of the 22 verses opens with the next letter of the Hebrew alphabet in strict sequence (22 of 22, per the skeleton-tier derivation table already computed for the book), an acrostic architecture that makes the poem's own internal shape -- not any external seam -- the boundary evidence for treating all twenty-two verses as one row. The petuchah at oshb:Prov.31.9 (single-witness, disclosed) is the poem's only bordering mark (1 of 1 interior/edge PE hit touching this span); ketiv/qere notes also touch this span at oshb:Prov.31.16 and oshb:Prov.31.18 (both disclosed), routine to the layer's density here and not evidence for any interior division.
rejected_alternative: Dividing the poem at its topical turn from the woman's own activities to her household's public praise was considered, but no address change marks that turn, and all 22 letters appear in strict alphabetic order (22 of 22, oshb:Prov.31.10-Prov.31.31) with no break at that topical midpoint, so splitting there would cut across the acrostic's own governing device rather than follow it.
